problem_statement: ShuvoMallick01/SKYBER-eCommerce-Website-HTML-Template is a static, multi-page eCommerce storefront (home index.html, product.html, shopping-cart.html, wishlist.html, blog.html, account and auth pages, plus the Seasonal Edit page seasonal-edit.html) that shares one header/footer, one main navigation and the css/style.css + css/helping.css design system (the --color-blue-500 accent, the grey scale tokens, the Poppins type and the rounded storefront components). The home page already lists product cards (.single-product) in the Featured Products grid. Give the storefront a first-class, genre-native 'Shop by category' product filter so a shopper can browse the catalogue by category. Above a product grid on the home page, ship a 'Shop by category' bar: a labelled row of category chips (All plus the storefront's own categories - Audio, Wearables, Cameras, Accessories - each with its product count) and a live readout that reports how many of the eight products are showing for the chosen category in the form 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>'. Promote a compact 'Shop focus' wayfinding marker across the browsing surfaces a shopper lands on (Home, Seasonal Edit AND Products). Ship the filter so it (1) advertises the marker on Home, Seasonal Edit AND Products (cross-page presence), (2) lays out its chip row responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) keeps the filtered product grid a tidy multi-column track with a legible active chip - never an overlapping pile of cards or a near-white-on-near-white illegible chip, and (4) keeps the readout in sync so a shopper who clicks the Audio chip sees the grid narrow to the two audio products and the readout update to 'Showing 2 of 8 . Audio' - it must re-read the live matched set, not show a stale captured count. Keep the rest of the storefront - the discount alert, the header search/account/wishlist/cart controls, the main navigation, the Summer Sale hero, the existing Featured Products / New Arrivals / category / support / latest-news sections, the product, cart, wishlist and blog pages, the footer, the local product imagery and the static HTTP behaviour - intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a 'Shop by category' filter bar above a product grid on the home page: a labelled chip row of All plus the storefront's own categories (Audio, Wearables, Cameras, Accessories), each showing its product count, and a live 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>' readout.
Promote a compact 'Shop focus' wayfinding marker so it renders on the Home, Seasonal Edit AND Products browsing surfaces (a shared marker, not a single-page copy).
The chip row must wrap responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Keep the filtered product grid a tidy multi-column track with a legible, high-contrast active chip; the active chip and card text must stay readable and the cards must never overlap into a pile.

Wire the chip clicks so that clicking a category (for example Audio) re-filters the grid to the matching products AND re-syncs the readout to 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>' (for example 'Showing 2 of 8 . Audio'); marking the chip active is not sufficient - the readout must re-read the live matched count, not a stale captured value.

Preserve the discount alert, header controls, main navigation, Summer Sale hero, the existing product/cart/wishlist/blog pages, the footer, the local product images and the static HTTP behaviour with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Drive the cross-page 'Shop focus' marker from the same shared markup on every browsing surface (Home, Seasonal Edit and Products) so one wayfinding cue reaches all three; do not paste a divergent copy on one page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The filter must adopt the storefront's design system (the --color-blue-500 accent for the active chip, the grey tokens, the rounded pill chips and Poppins type) so it reads as part of the site; the active chip must be legible (high-contrast accent fill), and the filtered grid must stay a tidy card track, not a negative-margin overlapping pile with near-white-on-near-white text.
Keep the readout in sync with the CURRENT category selection after every click by recomputing the visible count from the matched set, so it can never go stale relative to the shown cards.
Do not remove or regress the header, navigation, existing sections or other pages; use the storefront's in-repo local product images (no remote images or CDN dependencies).
state_constraints: desktop_home, tablet_home and mobile_home protect the storefront masthead across viewports and carry the cross-page 'Shop focus' marker on the Home page (D2 cross-page presence).

desktop_shopfilter, desktop_shopfilter_audio and mobile_shopfilter frame the Shop-by-category filter and product grid on the Home page; the reference keeps 0 overflow and a tidy grid, the negative controls overflow on mobile and (for the bad leg) collapse into an overlapping illegible pile of cards.
desktop_seasonal carries the cross-page 'Shop focus' marker on the Seasonal Edit page (present in the reference; the baseline omits it there).

desktop_products carries the cross-page 'Shop focus' marker on the Products page in the reference; the negative controls omit it there (baseline omits it everywhere but Home, the bad leg omits it on Products).
mobile_shopfilter is the horizontal-overflow discriminator: the reference reports 0 overflow while the fixed-width negative controls overflow the 390px phone.

change_completion: The Shop-by-category filter is present above the product grid on the Home page and the 'Shop focus' marker is promoted on Home, Seasonal Edit AND Products (the shared marker reaches all three).

After clicking the Audio category chip on the Home page, the grid narrows to the two audio products and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 2 of 8 . Audio' - the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 8 of 8 . All categories'.
design_consistency: The filter on the shopfilter states matches the reference's accent/grey storefront styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), with a legible active chip and a tidy card grid, not an overlapping pile or a near-white-on-near-white illegible chip.
The filter adopts the storefront's design tokens and rounded-pill idiom so it reads as part of the site across every surface.
responsive: No captured page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_shopfilter and tablet_home keep the filter and product grid readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The main navigation, header controls, the existing storefront sections and the product/cart/wishlist/blog pages remain present and functional.
The Seasonal Edit page, the footer, the local product images and the static HTTP behaviour are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add the storefront's own genre-native 'Shop by category' product filter across the Home page and the browsing surfaces with a live count readout, while keeping the header, navigation, other pages and the static site stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: static multi-page HTML/CSS eCommerce storefront with a shared header/nav/footer, a Featured Products grid on the home page, product/cart/wishlist/blog and account pages, a Seasonal Edit page, local product images and a css/style.css + css/helping.css design system
metadata.selected_repo_reason: ShuvoMallick01/SKYBER-eCommerce-Website-HTML-Template is a runnable static multi-page eCommerce storefront; it serves offline with no build step and hosts a natural design-continuity add on the storefront's OWN product grid and a Shop-by-category filter, spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page marker presence, filtered-grid layout, and chip-click count wiring.

author_notes: slot_298 rebuilt from an L2 add-a-page task to a genre-native L4 on the ShuvoMallick01 SKYBER-eCommerce-Website-HTML-Template static storefront. The lever is the storefront's OWN product grid and a native 'Shop by category' filter (All plus the storefront's own Audio / Wearables / Cameras / Accessories categories over eight real products, with a live 'Showing N of 8 . <Category>' readout), not a bolted-on metric rail. Each product card carries a real category (shared byte-identically across legs as the shopfilter section markup). The filter is hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the chip row uses a fixed-width non-wrapping 760px track that overflows a 390px phone; the reference wraps it. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the 'Shop focus' wayfinding marker must be promoted on Home, Seasonal Edit AND Products; the reference promotes it on all three, the baseline only on Home (so it fails the Seasonal and Products presence assertions) and the bad leg on Home + Seasonal (so it fails the Products presence assertion). Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad filtered grid collapses - the eight product cards are pulled together with large negative margins so they shingle into an illegible overlapping pile, the active chip is near-white text on a near-white fill and every card's text is near-white on a near-white card ground - failing pixelmatch/ssim/block fidelity against the tidy reference. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad chip click updates the active chip and re-filters the grid but the readout count was captured once at construction, so after the Audio click the readout stays 'Showing 8 of 8 . Audio'. Three leg-varying files (css/shopfilter.css, js/shopfilter.js and index.html for the marker whitelist) sit in suggested_files; the eight-product shopfilter section markup, the shared marker markup, the vendored Poppins/Font-Awesome fonts and the local product images are shared byte-identically across legs. Served offline as a static site (no build step) by a static file server with a real 404, with local product images and no network calls; that infrastructure is identical across legs.
